doc.title: Hubert Laws — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Arif Mardin's Flight
summary: Brown mentions a one-tune session on Arif Mardin's date; Laws doesn't remember it.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: The next listing in this discography, following In the Beginning – unless you want to say anything else about In the Beginning . . .
. . . there’s Arif Marden’s date under his name, or at least a session that recorded a tune entitled Flight.
There was one – there was only one tune.
I don’t remember that. Arif Marden?
And I played on that track called Flight.
Flight. You, Gary Burton, Jerry Friedman, Tony Levin on bass, rather interesting.
Wow. Son of a gun. I don’t remember that.

Then it said overdub, Phil Bodner, Joe Farrell, Bill Slapin, and then Romeo again. But you’re listed separately from them. You were listed out as on the original track, and then these folks overdubbed. Any words about Phil or Joe Farrell, some other folks who always seem to be in the section with you, who are also playing flute?
